success_patterns: First-turn openers that give only a destination plus an occasion (birthday, business conference) and name no service produce a single seek_information with no search and nothing saved. Cache comparison passes because the cache stays empty.
A first restaurant request with a city is a bare `search_restaurants(city=...)`, dropping descriptors like 'business lunch'. The result is assigned and saved as 'restaurants'.
A restaurant refinement (cuisine, rating) loads the cached 'restaurants' key and passes only the last message's kwargs ('at least 4.0' becomes rating=[4.0, 5]). Cached hotel keys are left alone.

A flight class reply with several flight keys cached (first_departure_flights, second_departure_flights, first_return_flights) gets one load/filter/save block per key. The same kwarg is used in every block and no hotel lines appear.
Code stays plain: every call is assigned and saved, with no imports, comments or prints. Key names are not scored, so any unused name works.

patch.reasoning: Nearly every success is already covered by the existing rules. The one gap is the destination-plus-occasion opener with no service named. It is not the flight-implying case in Rule 7, because there is no origin. In the batch it was handled correctly by emitting a lone seek_information. One short line pins this down and guards against the failure mode in the weakest 'success', where `<date>` placeholders were written into search calls. The meta-skill advises shrinking the skill, so this is a single compact insertion and does not add a new gate or example block.

edits.target: - Mention only MISSING MANDATORY parameters. Never ask for optional ones.
edits.content: - Destination-plus-occasion opener with NO service named and no dates ('a trip to Colorado Springs for my birthday', 'headed to Las Vegas for a business conference'): output ONE short seek_information (what they need, hotel dates or flight date) and nothing else. Never call search_* with placeholders such as '<date>'. Nothing is saved on that turn.
